title: Cutaneous amyloidosis (macular and lichen)
summary: Localised keratin-derived amyloid in the papillary dermis: rippled grey-brown patches on the upper back (macular) or very itchy firm papules on the shins (lichen), driven by chronic friction and scratching.

glance.think: Rippled grey-brown interscapular pigment, or itchy firm brown papules on the shins, in someone who scrubs or scratches.
glance.engine: Damaged keratinocytes → keratin-derived amyloid in the papillary dermis.
glance.backbone: Stop friction and scratching, potent steroid ± occlusion, emollients, treat itch; refer if refractory or unsure.
glance.never_miss: Systemic amyloidosis signs (purpura, macroglossia, nephrotic syndrome) are a different disease: refer.

what: **Macular and lichen amyloidosis** are localised cutaneous amyloidoses: rippled brown macules or itchy keratotic papules from chronic friction, often on the upper back or shins.

list: Amyloid: chronic scratching/friction deposits keratin-derived amyloid in the papillary dermis.
Amyloid: rippled “rippled” brown macular patches (interscapular) or lichenified papules on shins; itch can be severe.

diagnosis: Clinical, with biopsy and special stains (Congo red) when needed.

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Macular amyloid vs LPP / friction PIH

list: Stop scrubbing/loofahs; soft clothing; potent topical steroid ± occlusion or topical calcineurin inhibitor for itch.
Emollients; consider sedating antihistamine at night for sleep.
Refer if severe, diagnostic doubt, or for specialist options (retinoids, phototherapy).

red_flags: Systemic amyloid signs are a different disease — this page is localised cutaneous only.
